## Assessment as Transaction

![](friere-book.png){fig-align="center" alt="Listing from the TWU Norma Marion Alloway Library for the book 'Pedagogy of the Oppressed' by Paulo Freire."}

---


> Instead of communicating, the teacher issues communiqués and makes deposits which the students patiently receive, memorize, and repeat. This is the "banking" concept of education, in which the scope of action allowed to students extends only as far as receiving, filing, and storing the deposits. [@freirePedagogyOppressed1990, p. 72]



---




```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
Instructor -->> Learner: This is true. (deposit)
Learner ->> Instructor: Here is my paper! (payment)
Instructor -->> Learner: Here is your grade! (product)
Learner ->> Instructor: Here is another paper. (payment)
Instructor -->> Learner: Here is another grade. (product)
Instructor -->> Institution: Here is their final grade. 
Institution -->> Learner: Here is your final grade. (product)
Institution ->> Learner: Here are your credits. (product)
```



# Stop. Be outside. Think.

Recall a time when you were the *object* in an educational transaction, where 'teaching' or 'assessing' was something done **to** you. What might YOU do to avoid commoditizing grades in your practice?

## Agency in Assessment

::: {.notes}
What method of reporting assignment grades to learners best fits your current practice?
- percentage scale (e.g., 74%)
- raw score (e.g., 19/26)
- letter grade (e.g., A+, A, A- ... C-, D, F)
- proficiency scale (e.g. Excellent, Meets Expectations, Revision Needed, Not Assessable)
- a combination of the above
- other (please specify)
:::

---

Nominal
: named
: counts, mode

Ordinal
: named, ordered
: counts, mode, median

Interval
: named, ordered, equidistant
: counts, mean, median, mode, standard deviation

Ratio
: named, ordered, equidistant, true zero
